title: Constructibility of all reductions from the first one

proof.text: Put $t=\pi_E$, $B=\mathcal O_{E,X}$, $\Lambda_j=\mathcal O_E/t^j$ and $R_j=(\Lambda_j)_X$. The extension absolute value, DVR and finite-quotient lemmas give that every $\Lambda_j$ is finite. Apply the finite-coefficient model comparison to identify both constructibility conventions, retaining the same vanishing intervals.

source.place: Second paragraph: finite quotient rings and constructibility conventions.

proof.text: For the actual completed coefficient sheaf B, completed-coefficient regular quotients identify B/t^j with the fixed constant finite quotient, compatibly with the projection and all transitions. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution P of K. The site-versus-monoidal tensor comparison converts the resolution flatness to site flatness. Apply the flat successive-quotient tensor sequence in B-modules. The normalized quotient isomorphisms and the ordinary tensor-extension comparison identify its three terms with the actual scalar-extension complexes, restricted to B. Since the completed projection to the middle quotient is locally surjective, scalar restriction is full, faithful and exact. Lift the two maps and their short exactness to modules over that middle quotient. Its short-exact-sequence triangle, and the K-flat derived-extension counits, give the desired triangle with outer terms the restrictions of K_(n-1) and K_1 and middle term K_n. This is the coefficient-sequence argument of the blueprint, using the existing flat tensor construction directly rather than transporting an abstract derived quotient model.

source.place: Second paragraph: coefficient short exact sequences and their derived tensor triangles.

proof.text: Assume (1), choosing $r\le s$ with $H^q(K_1)=0$ outside $[r,s]$. Induct on $n\ge1$ with simultaneous claims: $K_n$ is bounded constructible and has this same bound. The base is (1). At $n>1$, [lem-pe-finite-scalar-restriction-constructible] puts both outer triangle terms in the bounded constructible category over the finite ring $\Lambda_n$, without changing bounds. The distinguished-triangle clause of [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated] gives constructibility of $K_n$. The long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] contains $H^q(\operatorname{Res}K_{n-1})\to H^q(K_n)\to H^q(\operatorname{Res}K_1)$. Outside $[r,s]$ both outer terms vanish, so exactness forces the middle term to vanish. This completes the induction and proves (2).

source.place: Second paragraph: induction, constructible extension closure and uniform interval.

proof.text: Use the fixed normalized integral section comparison and lem-pe-fixed-integral-section-squares. Localize its restriction squares and take their uniquely unit-compatible left-adjoint mates, as in lem-pe-integral-completion-presentation. The transition comparison identifies the full reduction towers. The section equivalence preserves and reflects products and distinguished triangles: forward canonical completeness is integral_completion_presentation, while reflection followed by lem-pe-internal-roos-completeness gives the reverse. For each finite level normalized ring isomorphisms are unique by sheafification, so lem-pe-finite-coefficient-model-comparison applies to the chosen encoding. Exact equivalences preserve homology and zero objects. Finite cohomological support together with the common interval is precisely bounded cohomology and the existing constructibility predicate in every degree. These arguments establish both directions of continuousIntegralConstructible_iff_sfIntegralConstructible for arbitrary K. The preceding induction now proves the first-reduction criterion, and the final two corollaries combine it with this integral interpretation.

source.place: Final sentence: interpreting all finite reductions in the existing complete integral category.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X$ be Noetherian, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite and $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$ derived
$\pi_E$-complete. Write $K_n=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\cO_{E,X}}(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$. The
following are equivalent:

1. $K_1\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E/\pi_E)$;
2. $K_n\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E/\pi_E^n)$ for every $n\ge1$, and the cohomology of the $K_n$ lies in
   one interval $[r,s]$ independent of $n$.

Combined with [sk-prop-integral-criterion], a derived $\pi_E$-complete $K$ lies in
$\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ if and only if (2) holds.

proof.text:
$(1)\Rightarrow(2)$. Suppose $K_1$ has cohomology in $[r,s]$, with constructible cohomology
sheaves. The exact sequences $0\to\cO_E/\pi_E^{n-1}\xrightarrow{\pi_E}\cO_E/\pi_E^n\to\cO_E/\pi_E\to0$
give, after $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}-$, distinguished triangles
$K_{n-1}\to K_n\to K_1\to K_{n-1}[1]$. By induction on $n$ and the long exact cohomology
sequence, $K_n$ has cohomology in $[r,s]$, and each $H^q(K_n)$ is an extension of a
subsheaf of $H^q(K_1)$ by a quotient of $H^q(K_{n-1})$: precisely, of
$\ker(H^q(K_1)\to H^{q+1}(K_{n-1}))$ by $\coker(H^{q-1}(K_1)\to H^q(K_{n-1}))$. With torsion
coefficients on a Noetherian scheme constructible sheaves are closed under kernels,
cokernels and extensions (the classical finite-stalk theory), regarding
$\cO_E/\pi_E$-modules as $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$-modules by restriction of scalars, which preserves
constructibility. Hence $H^q(K_n)$ is constructible and $K_n\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E/\pi_E^n)$, with
the uniform interval $[r,s]$.
